abstract: Whether the ageing cochlea follows the systemic ageing programmes defined by multi-organ atlases is unknown. We integrated single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data for 13,988 mouse cochlear nuclei (3, 12 and 24 months) with the Tabula Muris Senis atlas (16 droplet-based and 12 Smart-seq2 fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) sources). Cross-organ alignment of ageing programmes was quantified by genome-wide vector correlation, pre-ranked gene-set enrichment and a systemic ageing score. Cochlear ageing showed weak but significant genome-wide concordance with systemic ageing (Spearman rho 0.01-0.12), with lineage-matched pairs ranking among the highest. In contrast, systemic tissue ageing-up signatures, dominated by immune and inflammatory programmes, were depleted from the ageing-up rankings of cochlear non-sensory epithelial cells (normalised enrichment score -1.45, adjusted p = 0.032) and, for the immune-organ signatures, from cochlear macrophages. The cochlear macrophage ageing vector correlated positively with tissue-resident macrophages of peripheral organs (kidney rho = 0.056, 95% confidence interval 0.016-0.063, p = 1.6 x 10^-13; microglia rho = 0.034, p = 1.4 x 10^-6), negatively with bone-marrow and splenic macrophages, and not with lymphocytes. A systemic ageing score increased with age in spiral ganglion neurons, Schwann cells, inner hair cells, epithelial cells, and fibrocytes, but not in cochlear macrophages. These cell-type-resolved analyses support a compartmentalised view of cochlear ageing: non-immune compartments track systemic ageing weakly, the immune arm is reversed, and cochlear macrophages age along a tissue-resident rather than haematopoietic programme.

summary: Mouse cochlear single-nucleus RNA-seq across ages shows weak concordance with systemic ageing; cochlear macrophages age along a tissue-resident programme.
